speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you have progressive swelling and pain in your right ring finger; can you tell me exactly how long this has been going on and if the swelling comes and goes?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient reports that the pain and swelling in his right ring finger began 2 days ago while playing football. He recalls his finger got caught in the jersey of another player, who then pulled away forcefully.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Boutonniere Deformity due to Flexor Digitorum Profundus (FDP) tendon rupture.

The injury mechanism of the finger being forcibly pulled away while the patient was actively gripping it is classic for an FDP rupture. Given the acute onset and specific mechanism, a physical exam for the inability to flex the distal interphalangeal (DIP) joint is the critical next step to confirm the diagnosis.

DIAGNOSIS_READY_Answer: Rupture of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon at its point of insertion
